proposal.title: Industrial PhD Proposal: Real-Time Soft Sensors for Milk Quality and Fermentation Optimization in Dairy Production
proposal.summary: This three-year industrial PhD project bridges raw milk intake profiling with bioreactor control to stop next-day production losses in dairy manufacturing. By mapping farm-to-farm variables like somatic cell counts, fat, protein, and temperature to fermentation kinetics, the initiative introduces real-time soft sensors for yoghurt and cheese lines. The research pairs the dairy processing operations in Vojvodina with advanced biochemical engineering expertise from the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad.
proposal.problem: The dairy in Vojvodina runs yoghurt and cheese lines that suffer production losses because milk quality varies from farm to farm. Currently, these variations are only identified through lab tests the next day, preventing proactive intervention during processing.
researchQuestions: How can intake variables such as temperature, somatic cell counts, fat, and protein readings be mathematically mapped to fermentation outcomes in real time?
Can soft sensors combining intake parameters with mid-infrared spectroscopy and pH-stat base consumption predict lactic acid fermentation shifts before downstream processing failures occur?
What adaptive control algorithms can stabilize product quality across varying raw milk compositions in pilot-scale and industrial stirred-tank bioreactors?

plan.work: Collect historical and live intake data including temperature, somatic cell counts, fat, and protein readings alongside current fermentation performance metrics. Build initial multivariable regression and predictive models linking raw milk composition to acidification rates.
plan.result: A validated baseline dataset and preliminary predictive model correlating intake parameters with fermentation outcomes.

plan.work: Integrate intake-based predictive models with mid-infrared spectroscopy and pH-stat base consumption data using the faculty's 50 L and 150 L bioreactor infrastructure. Test adaptive control algorithms for early detection of fermentation anomalies.
plan.result: A functional soft sensor prototype tested at pilot scale capable of flagging problematic batches prior to acidification failure.

plan.work: Deploy and validate the soft sensor framework directly within the dairy production environment. Train plant personnel on real-time monitoring workflows and finalize the industrial PhD dissertation.
plan.result: An operational real-time monitoring system installed at the dairy and a completed industrial PhD thesis outlining the integrated soft sensing methodology.
